source_findings.statement: Eq.(52) defines p_k=exp(-Delta_k(rho)/v) and calls it the probability of elementary transition; p_k is used as a stochastic matrix entry in Eq.(51).
Eq.(50) applies hidden-crossing probability matrices on approach and receding sides of P_rot.
Eq.(55) calls P^Q_{beta,alpha}=exp(-2 Delta_{beta,alpha}/v) the associated single-pass transition probability.
Eq.(56) defines Delta_{beta,alpha} as the absolute value of a complex contour/action integral.
STCKLBR2 computes the Eq.(56) Stueckelberg parameter; program documentation says the resulting parameter file is used in subsequent calculations.
At Nmax=3, printed charge-exchange shell n=3 equals printed ionization at both 0.5 and 5 keV/amu.
CPC Eq.(43) prints Delta = pi DeltaE_min/(4 DeltaF) without a square on DeltaE_min.

cross_source_findings.statement: Richter & Solov'ev 1993 uses factor-two transition probability and prints Delta = pi (DeltaE_min)^2/(4 DeltaF).
CPC 2023 Eq.(43) differs from the 1993 advanced-adiabatic Landau-Zener/Stueckelberg formula by a missing square on the minimum gap. Do not silently correct the CPC source before author-code audit.

CPC Eq.(52) and Eq.(55) both use Stueckelberg-parameter language but differ by factor two in the exponent; inspected pages do not explicitly state Delta_k(Eq52)=Delta_betaalpha(Eq56) nor Delta_k=2 Delta_betaalpha.

derived_checks.statement: A complex-action amplitude with imaginary action Delta yields probability exp(-2 Delta/v).
Two uses of the reversible Eq.(51)-type stochastic block yield off-diagonal 2p(1-p), not p^2 in general; repeated encounter does not explain Eq.(55) factor two.

next_decisive_evidence: Static trace of public author ARSENY program package DOI 10.17632/n43srxwdnm.1 from Eq.(56)/STCKLBR2 data to CR_SECTION/transition probability exponent.
